title: Invertibility of the finite ordinary open restriction mate
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, an open immersion j:U→X, section-normalized coefficient operations o [def-sf-integral-open-operations], and a generator-normalized TensorComparison tensor. At any positive coefficient level indexed by n:N, transpose (tensor.ordinary n).inv under the ordinary integral-open and finite-open adjunctions. The resulting natural transformation finiteRestrictionMate: restriction⋙scalarReductionExtension_U(n) → scalarReductionExtension_X(n)⋙finiteRestriction(n) is invertible. No ordinary quotient model, strict system map, transition equation or system assembly is asserted.

source.place: Tags 03DJ and 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0941, ordinary quotient construction.

proof.text: Since j is a monomorphism, the actual pro-etale open object is subterminal. At each object of its slice, the extension-by-zero presheaf has a single summand. The summand injection and component projection are inverse, naturally in the slice object. The slice presheaf is therefore already a sheaf. Mathlib Over.forget.pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility and its unit equation show that the restriction of the global sheafification unit is invertible. The normalized localized adjunction unit is exactly the summand injection followed by this restricted unit, so it is invertible. Compose with the integral and finite coefficient-equivalence adjunctions; their units are isomorphisms as well.

Let epsilon be the ordinary integral counit at N. The right triangle identity and invertibility of the integral unit imply that restriction(epsilon) is invertible. The inverse integral coefficient equivalence is fully faithful, hence reflects isomorphisms, so epsilon.over(openObject j) is invertible. For any scalar-change presheaf, the restricted map at a slice object is ordinary extension of scalars of the corresponding section map of epsilon. Each such section map is an isomorphism, so the restricted scalar-change presheaf map is an isomorphism. Apply slice sheafification and transfer invertibility through Mathlib pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility, using NatIso.isIso_map_iff. The module-to-abelian-sheaf functor reflects isomorphisms. Finally transport through the object equalities and conjugation formula that specify scalarReductionExtension. This proves that the finite ordinary restriction of scalarReductionExtension(epsilon) is invertible.

Expand finiteRestrictionMate_app. The finite open unit is invertible by Step 1; finite restriction of inverse tensor.ordinary is invertible because functors preserve isomorphisms; the last factor is invertible by Step 2. Their composite is invertible. NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app assembles this componentwise result. No generator-normalization equation, projection square, finite-system assembly, or transition equation is needed for this invertibility assertion.
